request.spec:
The late charge is now worked out per 30-day boundary: for each full 30 days a claim is overdue,
the late percent in force on that boundary date (the due-by plus 30, 60, 90 ... days) of the
claim's figure, rounded like the claim, and the charges added up; a boundary whose percent is 0.00
adds nothing. A claim settled with its charge keeps the frozen figure.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The late charge is now worked out per 30-day boundary: for each full 30 days a claim is overdue,
the late percent in force on that boundary date (the due-by plus 30, 60, 90 ... days) of the
claim's figure, rounded like the claim, and the charges added up; a boundary whose percent is 0.00
adds nothing. A claim settled with its charge keeps the frozen figure.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text: A background wait loop I'd started to watch for `bin/e2e` was stopped when it hit its time limit. It never exited on its own because its `pgrep -f "bin/e2e"` check matched its own command line. That's harmless: the e2e run had already finished, with all 4 tests passing, so I won't restart it. The change is finished.
